summary: Werner Georg Kümmel was a religious studies scholar. He held academic posts at the University of Zurich (circa 1932–1951), Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (circa 1951–1952), and the University of Marburg (circa 1952–1973).
Werner Handt was an Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. in 1900 from the University of Tübingen, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Richard von Garbe from circa 1898 to 1900.

Werner Knobl specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Frankfurt, Paris, Mainz, Tübingen under Paul Thieme, and Leiden, where he earned a PhD. He held teaching posts at Kanazawa, Kyoto, Leiden, and several other Japanese universities.

Werner Schulemann worked in Tibetology and other fields. He earned a Dr.phil. at Breslau and a Dr.med. at Freiburg. He held posts at IG Farben (circa 1920–1936), the University of Düsseldorf (1931), and the University of Bonn (1938–1955).

Werner Sundermann was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He held posts at the Academy of Sciences of the GDR (circa 1970–1991), Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1970–1990), and Free University of Berlin (circa 1993–2000).

Werner Thomas was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied under Emil Sieg and Wolfgang Krause between 1947 and 1952, and later held a post at Goethe University Frankfurt from circa 1964 to 1988.
Wes Borton is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at East Carolina University, studied under Derek F. Maher, and was attested as a student at the University of Michigan in 2010.

Whalen Lai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned a BA at International Christian University and a Ph.D. at Harvard, and held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the University of California, Davis.

Whitelaw Ainslie was active in Indology and other fields. He served as an assistant surgeon (1788) and surgeon (1794–1815) for the East India Company, and became a Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh in 1829.

Whitley Stokes was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at St Columba's College, earned a B.A. from Trinity College Dublin (1846–1851), and studied under Carl Siegfried and Rudolf Thomas Siegfried.

Whitney Cox works in Indology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Virginia and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock and others, Cox held posts at SOAS University of London and the University of Chicago.

Widi Widiyanto is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Widiyanto completed degrees at Sekolah Tinggi Agama Buddha Maha Prajna and Universitas Hindu Indonesia, and was appointed Dosen Tetap at STIAB Jinarakkhita in 2022.

Wijesinghe Sugathadasa Karunaratne worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ceylon and SOAS University of London. He held posts at the University of Ceylon, the University of Peradeniya, and the University of Kelaniya.

Wiktor Jan Porzeziński worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Moscow State University under Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov and taught there from 1903 to 1921, later holding professorships at the University of Warsaw and the Catholic University of Lublin.
Wilber Theodore Elmore was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Nebraska-Lincoln by 1915 and taught at Palmer Theological Seminary in 1925.

Wilbur Stone Deming was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Brown University and Boston University, joined the American Marathi Mission in 1912, and served as Superintendent of the American Mission High School, Ahmednagar, in 1924.

Wilburn Hansen is a scholar in religious studies and Japanology. Hansen completed a master's program at the University of Colorado Boulder, studied at Stanford University, and was taught by Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt.

Wilfred Cantwell Smith was a religious studies scholar educated at Toronto, Cambridge, and Princeton. He taught at Forman Christian College and held professorships and directorships at McGill University, Harvard University, and Trinity College, Toronto.

Wilfred Harvey Schoff was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Harvard and the University of Pennsylvania, served at the Philadelphia Commercial Museum, and was a visiting lecturer at Wisconsin-Madison (1901) and Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1903).

Wilfrid Sellars was a philosopher who studied at Michigan, Buffalo, Göttingen, and Oxford. He taught at the University of Iowa, the University of Minnesota Twin Cities, Yale University, and held a professorship at the University of Pittsburgh from 1963 to 1989.
